item.title: Jared Goff: I love it when the vultures come out
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The first two weeks of the Lions' season haven't painted the picture of a team firing on all cylinders.
item.content:encoded:
The first two weeks of the Lions' season haven't painted the picture of a team firing on all cylinders.

Week 1 saw them give up a 21-0 lead to the Saints before rallying for a win in overtime and they fell down by 21 points during a 41-31 loss in Buffalo in Week 2. That's led to plenty of doubts about the team's ability to contend at a high level this season, but quarterback Jared Goff said that is just fine with him because he thinks it will bring the best out of the team.

"I'm excited to get back home and play in front of our fans for sure, but you love when the vultures start coming out," Goff said. "Guys' character really emerges and I know our guys in this locker room and you can see those guys stand tall and be who they are. Stand in the fire, take the shots and fight right through it. . . . We're in a great place. Excited to get back in front of our fans."

A win over the Jets this Sunday would keep the vultures at bay, but a loss would probably make Goff and company a little less comfortable with how they're situated heading into October.

item.title: Jameis Winston: Being a starting quarterback is what I dream of
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants are looking at their options for adding a quarterback in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, but it's Jameis Winston's show for now.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants are looking at their options for adding a quarterback in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, but it's Jameis Winston's show for now.

Winston replaced Dart when he was injured in Monday night's loss to the Rams and he's set to start against the Titans in Week 3. It's not Winston's first time in the role and he started two games when Dart was injured in 2025, but he called the prospect of getting almost an entire season in the role for the first time since leaving the Bucs after the 2019 season "a beautiful opportunity" to show what he's capable of doing.

"This is what I've always dreamed of, to be a starting quarterback," Winston said, via a transcript from the team. "Obviously, my respects and gratitude is just going to be with Jaxson, but at the same time, this is what I dream of. I dream of being what I am right now and executing at a high level."

Winston did not play well against the Rams, but said he is "very confident in my ability to execute with precision" in the weeks to come. With games against the Titans, Cardinals and Commanders in the next three weeks, the Giants will need that to happen immediately or their hopes of doing more than simply surviving the season won't be in great shape.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes: We have to keep the hunger we had all offseason
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Through two weeks, the Chiefs have looked like they're back.
item.content:encoded:
Through two weeks, the Chiefs have looked like they're back.

At 2-0, Kansas City leads the league in yards and is No. 3 in scoring. It's a stark contrast to what the team displayed last year, even before quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered an ACL tear. And then, of course, the club finished 6-11.

But even with the success of the first two weeks, Mahomes said in his Wednesday press conference that Kansas City can't start feeling too good about itself for a hot start.

"I think more than anything [about] who we're playing is just staying hungry,” Mahomes said, via transcript from the team. “In this league, it's week to week. One week they're patting you on your back, and one week they're telling you you're terrible. I think all offseason we heard about how bad we were, and guys were super hungry and came in with that mentality, and I think that's why we've had the success that we've had these first two weeks. And it's like, how can you keep that hunger? Now everybody's saying we're amazing and that we're great, and it's like we've got to keep the hunger that we've had this entire offseason.

“So that's what we're preaching, is like we're nowhere near where we want to be at. We're still so early in the season, and there's still so much for us to learn from and so much for us to get better at, and we have to have that mentality week in and week out if we want to go out there and have success.”

Part of that is harping on the details to make sure the team is capitalizing on all of its opportunities.

“I think as an offense you saw, I mean, we had more opportunities to score touchdowns,” Mahomes said. “We kicked some field goals there in the red zone, and it came down to just the little things with miscommunications or route depth or me not making the right read and getting to the right guy at the right time. Those are the little things you have to continue to get better and better at, because you don't know how many of those opportunities you're going to get when you're in the red zone.

“I love kicking field goals and they're three points, but touchdowns are so big in this league, and you want to make sure that you can actually get those. We have to get better at that of executing kind of in the red zone and getting those touchdowns because that's what wins you football games.”

The Chiefs will take on the Dolphins in Miami on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

item.title: Ronde Barber: "Mood is not great" at Buccaneers headquarters
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Buccaneers are 0-2, capped by a 23-19 loss to the Browns in the Tampa Bay home opener.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers are 0-2, capped by a 23-19 loss to the Browns in the Tampa Bay home opener. And the sluggish start is having an impact.

Via JoeBucsFan.com, Hall of Famer Ronde Barber said this week that the vibe in the building is not ideal.

“Look, the mood is not great,” Barber said on his WFLA show. ”There’s too many mistakes. There’s a lack of urgency, if you will, in my mind when I look at them going onto the field. There’s got to be a little bit of a sense of a defining characteristic of your team through Week 2. I don’t know what that is. It’s mistakes. It’s busts. It’s lack of execution.”

Barber believes the Bucs simply weren't ready for the games that count.

“Week 2 can’t be the fifth preseason game,” Barber said. “At some point you have to start hitting your stride. And it doesn’t feel like they’re in their stride right now on either side of the ball.”

“I feel like for much of the secondary, especially the coverage unit, they’re so focused on what they’re trying to do that they don’t know how to do it now.”

Barber also singled out former Lions linebacker Alex Anzalone, who signed with the Bucs as a free agent.

“There’s some dynamic going on, whether it’s not understanding what his role is in the defense, not understanding angles, maybe not having enough tackles in the preseason, I don’t know what it is,” Barber said. ”Something is hamstringing this defense in critical moments."

It puts even more pressure on the Buccaneers for Week 3, the second of three straight home games. The official attendance last week was 61,391 — nearly 8,000 below capacity. (Often, the actual attendance is lower than the reported number.)

By the time the game was over, the fans who stuck it out through the lengthy weather delay weren’t happy. Those who show up for the next game will be even saltier if the Bucs slip to 0-3.

That makes it a dangerous game for the Vikings, who have overachieved to get to 2-0. This is exactly the kind of game in which the team that has done better than expected can step into a pothole against a team that has done worse than expected.

item.title: This week's NFL officiating video reminded teams not to line up offside on the tush push
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The NFL is reminding teams not to line up offside on the tush push.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is reminding teams not to line up offside on the tush push.

In a video sent to all 32 teams this week, NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson used a Seahawks tush push, which was called for offensive offside, to illustrate the type of penalty that will be called.

"We have covered this before, but clubs are reminded on both sides of the ball to line up properly on these push plays," Anderson said.

Anderson showed how the Seahawks were aligned on the play, which was snapped to tight end AJ Barner for a first down but called back because of the penalty, and said one Seahawk had both his hand and helmet in the neutral zone, and another had his hand in the neutral zone.

"Here, this hand is clearly offside, this head is clearly offside, as is the right hand of the tight end," Anderson said.

During the unsuccessful attempt to ban the tush push in 2025, one of the arguments against it was that it was too hard to officiate. The league is still trying to make sure everyone understands exactly what will and will not be flagged.

item.title: Packers rule out LG Aaron Banks, list DT Javon Hargrave as questionable for Thursday night
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Packers released their final injury report for Thursday night's game against the Falcons and it confirms that they'll be without two starting offensive linemen for the game.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers released their final injury report for Thursday night's game against the Falcons and it confirms that they'll be without two starting offensive linemen for the game.

Left guard Aaron Banks (knee, toe) has been ruled out after leaving last Sunday's win over the Jets in the second quarter. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele tore his patellar tendon in that game and is out for the season.

Guard Donovan Jennings (hand) and tackle Anthony Belton (elbow) replaced them last week and both are set to play as they did not receive injury designations.

Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (knee, concussion) is questionable after missing Week 2. Defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) is also listed as questionable.

Wide receiver Jayden Reed was officially ruled out with the neck injury that caused him to spend time in a New Jersey hospital before returning to Green Bay during the week. Defensive tackle Warren Brinson (calf) will miss the game as well.

item.title: George Pickens is "happy" despite nine catches for 68 yards through two games
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: In a contract season, Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens is looking for an encore to his 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns last season.
item.content:encoded:
In a contract season, Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens is looking for an encore to his 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns last season.

He has only nine catches for 68 yards through two games, with two drops. CeeDee Lamb leads the team with 13 receptions for 197 yards and three touchdowns.

"Long as we score, and as long as we're winning, me personally, if I'm blocking or if I'm setting a crack block and that engineered the 37 points, I’m happy," Pickens said Wednesday, via Tommy Yarrish of the team website.

Pickens' numbers aren't far off the start to his 2025 season when he made eight catches for 98 yards and a touchdown in the first two games.

"Of course I want to get him and CeeDee the ball," Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I think CeeDee is playing great. I think George is playing really well. Some of the catches he made [against Washington] were really big-time plays in big-time situations for us. . . . He draws a lot of attention out there. But believe me, we're looking for ways to continue to get those guys the ball.

"If you look at George last year, he didn't take off until a couple games in. And the rest, as they know, is history how well he played. I have no questions about him and his readiness. He'll be ready to go this week."

Pickens agrees that he is playing well despite how the numbers look.

"I'd definitely say team for me. I feel like I've been doing great," Pickens said. "As far as the team, like my whole game. Some people just look at certain parts of my game. My whole game I feel like has been great."

item.title: Brian Burns likely to miss time with low ankle sprain
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Giants pass rusher Brian Burns said after Monday night's loss to the Rams that his low ankle sprain was "nothing serious."
item.content:encoded:
Giants pass rusher Brian Burns said after Monday night's loss to the Rams that his low ankle sprain was "nothing serious." But it is probably serious enough to keep him out at least this week.

Burns is likely to miss some time, according to Adam Schefter.

The 28-year-old Burns is one of the Giants’ best defensive players, losing him was a big blow, on a night when the offense suffered an even bigger blow with the loss of quarterback Jaxson Dart, who will miss the rest of the regular season with a knee injury.

The Giants traded for Burns in 2024 and signed him to a five-year, $141 million contract. He has started every game for the Giants since then, and last year he had a career-high 16.5 sacks.

item.title: Marvin Harrison Jr.: My process won't change whether I get 0 catches or 10 catches
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has only caught one pass through two games this season.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has only caught one pass through two games this season. But he doesn't think he needs to change anything.

Asked if he's losing confidence, Harrison said he knows he's preparing the right way, and that's all that matters.

"Does your confidence come from results or does your confidence come from your process?" Harrison said, via ESPN. "And I think for me it comes from my process. So, my process isn’t going to change whether I get zero catches or 10 catches. I'm going to still do the same thing week in and week out, Monday through Saturday to prepare myself for games. So, I think that's where I have a lot of my confidence comes from. And obviously you want to have more of an impact in the game, but I think confidence really has to come from preparation more than anything."

Harrison said no one player is ever solely responsible for his own production.

"It's definitely a combination of a lot of things," Harrison said. "For my route tree getting down the field, you need a lot of things to go right. You need the right coverage, you need protection to hold up, you need me to run a great route, you need obviously Jacoby to make the right pass and make the right read. So, I feel like it's never one person's fault for anybody's success or lack thereof, really. So, I think it's always a combination of a bunch of things and whether that's a lack of success or success in general."

Harrison's comments may be true, and yet there's no denying that he has been a disappointment as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft. His rookie year was only OK, he declined in his second season, and through two games in Year 3 he has gone into a steeper decline. Harrison's process may not change, but something has to change.

item.title: Jaxson Dart could return for the postseason, if the Giants qualify
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: John Harbaugh confirmed Jaxson Dart will need surgery to repair his knee injury, but the Giants coach couched how long the quarterback might be out.
item.content:encoded:
John Harbaugh confirmed Jaxson Dart will need surgery to repair his knee injury, but the Giants coach couched how long the quarterback might be out.

"Regular season at least, I would say," Harbaugh said, via video from SNY Giants.

Asked a follow-up question about whether he was leaving open the possibility of Dart returning for the postseason, if the Giants qualify, Harbaugh said: "I think I said it. I said it. Regular season. Other than that, how do you know? There's no way to know. It depends on the recovery. You can't pinpoint it exactly."

Dart's absence, though, decreases the Giants' chances of getting to the playoffs.

Dart, who was injured in Monday night's loss to the Rams, will undergo surgery to repair damage to the MCL and the meniscus in his left knee, according to multiple reports.

The Giants initially believed Dart's injury was not season-ending, but the MRI delivered the bad news, and he will undergo surgery soon.

"It's a big loss for sure. It's your starting quarterback," Harbaugh said.

Dart was in team meetings on Wednesday, while trying to come to terms with the fact that his third season is over after only two games.

"I think he's determined," Harbaugh said. "He's bummed. It's hard. The season's not over, but it is for him. We kind of talked about that, too. That was part of it. There's a certain mourning that takes place."

Jameis Winston will take over as the starter, though the Giants are in the market for a veteran quarterback to join Jake Haener behind Winston. Harbaugh said his message to the team was "it's not a one-game man."

"We need to be the best Giants we can be," he said.

item.title: John Harbaugh: All options are open for adding a veteran QB
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Jaxson Dart will miss at least the rest of the regular season with his knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
Giants coach John Harbaugh confirmed starting quarterback Jaxson Dart is out for the regular season. Jameis Winston will assume the role of starter, but Harbaugh said the Giants will add another quarterback.

"We will," Harbaugh said, via video from SNY Giants. "We plan on doing that, absolutely. Can't say who at this point. We're working on that."

Harbaugh, who said he prefers adding a veteran, did not rule out acquiring a quarterback via trade.

"All options are open," Harbaugh said, via Jordan Raanan of ESPN.

Jake Haener is the Giants' only other healthy quarterback besides Winston, and Haener's only experience is eight games, including one start, with the Saints in 2024.

Earlier today on PFT, Mike Florio laid out the options the Giants have for adding a veteran quarterback.

item.description: Last Thursday night, Bills receiver DJ Moore left the home opener against the Lions with a shoulder injury.
item.content:encoded:
Last Thursday night, Bills receiver DJ Moore left the home opener against the Lions with a shoulder injury. On the first full day of practice in advance of the Week 3 home game against the Chargers, Moore made a move toward returning.

Moore was listed as practicing on a limited basis. Given the very broad nature of the "limited" category, it's hard to know whether that means he'll be good to go in four days.

Also injured from the Buffalo receiving corps is Keon Coleman. He did not practice on Wednesday, with an ankle injury.

The Bills also were missing a pair of starting defensive tackles. Ed Oliver didn't practice due to the hip injury that made him a late scratch on Thursday night. Defensive tackle T.J. Sanders underwent an appendectomy on Tuesday night.

In Week 1, Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Texans. He had no catches in his 23 snaps from Week 2. Coleman had one catch for one yard in Week 1, and six catches for 63 yards on six targets in Week 2.

item.title: Kyle Hamilton: Think we have a great plan to keep Brazil travel from hindering us
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: There was a lot of focus on travel plans leading into the Week 1 game between the 49ers and Rams in Australia, but there's been less attention paid to the Ravens and Cowboys as they prepare to play in Rio this week.
item.content:encoded:
There was a lot of focus on travel plans leading into the Week 1 game between the 49ers and Rams in Australia, but there's been less attention paid to the Ravens and Cowboys as they prepare to play in Rio this week.

There's good reason for that as it is a much less severe time difference for both teams, but there's still an overnight flight for both teams on Thursday night and that will be different than other games that take place in different time zones. On Wednesday, Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said that he thinks the team has a good handle on how to approach Sunday's game.

"I think the staff — credit to everybody involved — has a great plan in place for us when we get down there, and [we are] going to try to take advantage of the travel in a way that it is not hindering us coming into Sunday," Hamilton said, via the team's website. "I think the words 'flying out of our skin' were used in the team meeting, so that is the ultimate goal. Obviously, both sides are dealing with it, so there are really no excuses to be made but, I think we have a good plan in place and good organization when we get down there."

The interest in the travel plans for the Australia game was piqued by the different approaches that the two teams took to the trip. With the Cowboys and Ravens following the same schedule, it's unlikely to be much of a talking point after the game either.

item.title: Darius Slayton: Daniel Jones and I see field similarly, expect that to work well for us
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Darius Slayton was watching last Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs, which meant he saw Colts wideout Alec Pierce leave the game after aggravating a heel injury.
item.content:encoded:
Darius Slayton was watching last Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs, which meant he saw Colts wideout Alec Pierce leave the game after aggravating a heel injury.

Slayton said on Wednesday that he "wasn't cheering for that," but he knew that Pierce's injury might create an opportunity for him to land his first job since being released by the Giants this summer. Not only did the Colts have an immediate need for receiver help, they also have Slayton's former Giants teammate Daniel Jones as their quarterback.

That history likely played a role in Slayton signing with the Colts this week and he said he expects to get right back into a groove with the quarterback.

"Really enjoyed playing alongside him," Slayton said, via the team's website. "He's a good quarterback. He's smart. He can spin it. . . . Philosophically, I think we see the field pretty similarly, and that's something that worked well for us in the past. And I expect it to work well for us going forward."

Pierce averaged more than 20 yards a catch in each of the last two seasons, but Slayton has not been that kind of wideout during his time in the NFL so the Colts will have to adapt their offense to the players available as they try to find their first win of the season.

item.title: Mike Vrabel, Drake Maye address the balance between decisiveness and recklessness
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After a Week 2 win over the Steelers, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel didn't want to have his Sunday "ruined" by questions about the performance of quarterback Drake Maye.
item.content:encoded:
After a Week 2 win over the Steelers, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel didn't want to have his Sunday "ruined" by questions about the performance of quarterback Drake Maye. Vrabel also didn't seem to want to have his Wednesday ruined by them, either.

Asked during his midweek press conference whether the pendulum for Maye "maybe swung too far back in the other direction" from being overly aggressive in Week 1 against the Seahawks (when he had three game-killing fourth-quarter interceptions) to being too careful in Week 2 against the Steelers, Vrabel didn't seem to be thrilled with the inquiry.

"Again, these are questions that I would like to answer on Monday," Vrabel said. "I think I was willing to do that. The focus has got to be on Jacksonville and our performance. Whether it’s the pendulum — it’s being decisive in everyone's play, but it’s certainly magnified with the quarterback. So being decisive, believing in what you see. Again, that’s what we ask all our players to do is prepare to try to play fast and aggressively and make great decisions. So, yeah, we could always say, 'Man, we should have let that one rip,' or 'We’ve got to make a better decision.' Ultimately, it’s his responsibility to be able to distribute the football as quickly and decisively as possible in the places that it’s supposed to go, continue not to force things and try to just create a next play on every single play."

Maye's midweek press conference opened with a question regarding the importance of not overthinking and playing freely on the field.

"One of the best things about getting new chances every week is having to let the other ones go," Maye said. "That's one of the best things about this sport and playing this position. You’ve got to let plays go, and you want to be attacking the next play, learning from the ones in the past and getting after the next one. So, I definitely think, this job, it's hard to play this position when you’re thinking about a lot of different things, and you are going to be regardless. It's going to be natural to think about motions, fronts, defenses, what our guys are doing, route concept and what they’re doing versus the play we have up. So, just thinking and trying to be instinctive. That's one of the best things I learned in college is to be instinctive and try to play as fast as you can back there."

Maye later was asked about Vrabel's comments on the importance of decisiveness and believing what he sees.

"I think that goes back to playing instinctive, seeing it, trusting what I see in practice, trusting the decisions I’m making out there on the field," Maye said. "I’ve never shied away from trusting something and letting it rip. So, just knowing what I’m seeing, seeing it in front of the guys, and at the same time, giving our guys a chance to make a play. Sometimes, when you do that, you end up forcing the football into decisions that you maybe want back by trying to give your guys a chance to go make a play. So, realizing that, and also keeping the chains moving is just as important to get those next chances to push the ball down the field."

Through two games in 2026, something is off. To the extent passer rating matters, Maye's has fallen from 113.5 in 2025 to 63.1 in 2026. He had 31 touchdown passes and eight interceptions last year. This year, he has one touchdown pass and four interceptions.

With upcoming games at Jacksonville and Buffalo, it's an opportunity to turn the clock back a year. If not, an ugly early-season narrative could start taking root.

item.title: Kurt Warner: I played through a dislocated left elbow, Jayden Daniels can if he wants to
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Warner injured his left elbow in 2007 and returned the next week wearing a large brace.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner says Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels could play through the left elbow injury he suffered on Sunday.

Warner, who now appears on ESPN, described suffering the same injury in 2007 and not missing a game.

“I suffered the exact same injury back in ’07, and I played the next week," Warner said. "I braced it up, obviously a couple shots along the way, I had to hand the football off with my right hand in both directions, but this to me is something, because it's the left arm, if he wants to play through that, and get back out there and help his team, I believe he can. It's not going to be one of those things that affects the throwing part of things. Does it affect his movement, does it affect his running or some of the things they want to do by design? Maybe, but I do believe this is something he can come back from. Because it's the left arm, I don't think it's something we worry about long term and go, 'Should we extend this guy, because he's had this type of injury twice?' I believe it's something he can play through."

Warner said that as a player, his mentality would be to do everything he can to help his team win.

"I can brace it up and go," Warner said. "I don't care about all that stuff. Let me go out there and play, I want to be out there with my guys as opposed to thinking about this a year or two down the road."

Warner suffered his left elbow injury in Week 6 of 2007 when he was sacked by Panthers defensive end Julius Peppers. Warner missed the rest of that game, and when the injury was initially diagnosed he was expected to miss more time, but instead he played in Week 7, wearing a large brace on his left elbow, and started every game for the Cardinals the rest of the season. Warner played well down the stretch and was named the starter in 2008 after starting 2007 as the backup to Matt Leinart, and in 2008 Warner led the Cardinals to the Super Bowl.

What's unknown is whether Warner is correct to call his injury "the exact same injury" that Daniels had. Daniels' left elbow injury may be more severe, and it may not be feasible for him to play, even with a heavy brace on his left elbow. Warner displayed incredible toughness, but that doesn't necessarily make it the right decision for Daniels.

item.title: Justin Herbert disputes perception of lack of vocal leadership
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Something has kept Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert from fulfilling a skillset that has had coach Jim Harbaugh proclaim that Herbert will be regarded as the best to ever play the game.
item.content:encoded:
Something has kept Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert from fulfilling a skillset that has had coach Jim Harbaugh proclaim that Herbert will be regarded as the best to ever play the game. The disconnect between talent and production has become more pronounced in the early days of the 2026 season, given that the Chargers have lost a pair of home games to two of the worst teams in the league in 2025.

On Wednesday, Herbert's midweek press conference included questions about a potential increase in vocal leadership.

In response to the first — regarding the possible need for vocal leadership in advance of the Week 3 game at Buffalo — Herbert bristled.

"I think that would imply that there's no need for vocal leadership before this week," Herbert said, via Kris Rhim of ESPN. "I think every week is a super important week for us and it's a great opportunity for us to go play football again and correct the things that we made mistakes on last week and keep pushing forward."

Herbert interrupted the second question on the subject.

"I don't think there's a lack of vocal leadership at all," Herbert said. "So, I'm going to stop you right there and say that it's very present. I don't think anyone is panicked or worried because that's not going to be the sentiment. It's moving on to the next play and understand that we're close, we've made mistakes, how do we fix it?"

Herbert reiterated his expectation that there will be no panic, as the team stares at the possibility that 0-2 will become 0-3 and, based on the upcoming schedule (at Seahawks, Broncos, at Chiefs), possibly 0-6 at the bye.

Regardless, something is missing. And it it's not an issue of Herbert's talent, it's something else. Perhaps the players around him aren't good enough. Perhaps he's not doing enough to get more out of them. Perhaps the odd-couple pairing of Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is a work in progress that has yet to make enough progress.

A win will change everything. But the team looked flat and overmatched in two straight games the Chargers should have won. Now comes the gauntlet, and there's a chance the hole will get deeper and deeper with each passing week.

item.title: Commanders push back on narrative they abandoned Jayden Daniels
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Commanders franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels was injured on the final play of the first half.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels was injured on the final play of the first half. As team medical personnel worked on his dislocated left elbow, Daniels' teammates were seen on the Fox broadcast walking by him toward the locker room.

Commanders players pushed back against the social media narrative that they abandoned their quarterback.

"It’s bullshit what people are saying," Washington left tackle Brandon Coleman said, via John Keim of ESPN. "Jay's our guy, and he's been our guy. There's no malice behind it."

Many players stayed on the sideline watching Daniels being attended to, per Keim, and many returned to his side after trainers popped Daniels' elbow back in place.

Coach Dan Quinn said what actually happened was the "opposite" of the narrative that grew from Fox's short clip.

"When the half is over, the referees are saying, 'Man, I can't delay the half. They can't stay on the field,' The players were like, 'No, we want to stay,'" Quinn said. "So it's just the opposite of that. They were gutted. They love this guy. So halftime was hard and emotional in that space."

Coleman and lineman Josh Conerly Jr. were the last players to leave for the locker room, along with Quinn and backup quarterbacks Marcus Mariota and Athan Kaliakmanis.

"All that stuff is ridiculous," tight end Ben Sinnott said. "As far as the love and brotherhood we have for Jayden, it's really strong. We've seen how hard he worked to get to where he's been.

"It was a weird situation. People were trying to figure out what's going on, and they wanted to give the trainers space to do it. You don't want to crowd the guy. Obviously, guys are taking a step back and giving him space, praying, and we all came back.

"All that stuff is nonsense."

item.title: Case Keenum ready to start for Bears if needed
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bears haven't named Case Keenum the starter for Monday night's game against the Eagles, but he could be the next man up.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears haven't named Case Keenum the starter for Monday night's game against the Eagles, but he could be the next man up.

Keenum was the only quarterback on the active roster to practice Wednesday, with Caleb Williams rehabbing a hamstring injury and Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol. Miller Moss, an undrafted rookie on the Bears' practice squad, took the backup reps to Keenum.

Keenum has started 66 games but none since Dec. 24, 2023, against the Browns. That was also the last game he saw action.

"I feel very prepared," Keenum said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "It's what I do every week. It's what I've done for a long time. I've backed up a long time in this league. If my name's called, I'm excited to be out there."

Keenum, 38, has played for eight different teams since entering the NFL in 2012. He is 3-0 as a starter against Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.

Keenum has thrown for 15,175 yards and 79 touchdowns.

Coach Ben Johnson, formerly the Lions' offensive coordinator, has never called plays for a backup quarterback, and both Jared Goff and Caleb Williams were No. 1 overall picks. Keenum was an undrafted free agent but with experience.

"He's been a baller from the day he was born from what I can tell," Johnson said. "He's got that way about him. He's got a knack. His teammates gravitate to him. I think that's a good starting point for a quarterback. And of course he's up there in years a little bit, but that experience has really paid off for him. He sees the game the same way we do. I think he accelerates through his progressions, because he's seen so many things over the course of his time. He's been in so many different offenses.

"So in a lot of ways, he might be a step slower than he was when he first entered the league, and yet his mind is going so fast it helps catch him on up. And he's playing as good of football as he probably has his entire career, is what he'd tell you."

item.title: Jacoby Brissett: No one has lost confidence in Marvin Harrison Jr.
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Marvin Harrison Jr. hasn't been the wide receiver the Cardinals thought they were getting when they drafted him fourth overall in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
Marvin Harrison Jr. hasn't been the wide receiver the Cardinals thought they were getting when they drafted him fourth overall in 2024. That's something everyone can agree.

The Cardinals, though, are pushing back against the narrative surrounding Harrison's slow start to 2026.

A viral video, viewed more than 18 million times, started the discussion about Harrison's effort level. Other videos have since questioned whether Harrison is giving 100 percent.

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett and coach Mike LaFleur defended Harrison on Wednesday.

“When you talk about his work ethic and you talk about him showing up and being engaged in the meetings and then going out on the field and giving 110 percent and being the Marv we all know he is, that hasn’t changed,” Brissett said, via Tyler Drake of Arizona Sports.

“Nobody’s lost confidence in Marv. The hard part as a young player is the noise from the outside telling you what they expect from you and the things of that nature. Does Marv want the ball? Yes. Do we understand that he wants the ball? Yes. Is it only Week 2? Yes. . . . At some point, the tide will change. When? We don’t know yet. Hopefully soon.”

Harrison has seen four targets, with one catch for 33 yards this season.

LaFleur was asked on Monday about Harrison jogging through routes.

“I don’t see it that way. I think his running style is different from some other people’s,” LaFleur said. “If that’s people’s narrative on him, that’s fine, but I know his teammates don’t feel that way.”

LaFleur doubled down Wednesday.

"In between those walls, Marv is Marv,” he said. “He’s attacking it every single day like he always does, just like his teammates do. I appreciate the way he goes about his business.”

As for whether Harrison’s run-blocking needs to improve, LaFleur said everyone’s “efforts need to improve.”

Dan Graziano of ESPN talked to league executives who wondered whether the Cardinals will shop Harrison before the trade deadline. The Texans are among the teams that could be in the market for help at the position.

item.title: Antonio Brown plans to take plea deal in attempted murder case
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Former NFL receiver Antonio Brown will not be going to prison for attempted murder.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL receiver Antonio Brown will not be going to prison for attempted murder.

Via David Fischer of the Associated Press, Brown plans to accept a plea deal. He'll plead guilty to a lesser charge and serve no time.

Per the report, attorney Mark Eiglarsh said Brown plans to plead no contest to aggravated assault on September 30. He will be sentenced to probation and the adjudication will be withheld. That prevents Brown from being regarded as a convicted felon.

It means that Brown will be pleading no contest to a felony.

He originally faced up to 30 years in prison for an incident that occurred at a celebrity boxing match in May 2025. Brown allegedly grabbed a handgun from a security officer and fired two shots at a man who allegedly had attacked Brown.

Brown had left the country after the incident. He was eventually apprehended and returned to the U.S. to face the charges.

“This was not an easy decision,” Eiglarsh said in a statement issued Wednesday. “Antonio believes in his innocence. He believes strongly in his Stand Your Ground defense, and he believes he would ultimately prevail at trial. But when prosecutors put an offer on the table that transforms a potential decades-long prison sentence into a significantly reduced charge and probation, there was simply no way he could reasonably turn it down.”

Brown is eligible for enshrinement in the Hall of Fame in 2027. Off-field issues aren't supposed to be considered. It remains to be seen how the newly reconfigured Hall of Fame voting panel will handle his candidacy.

A 12-year veteran, Brown earned first-team All-Pro status in four straight seasons. He qualified for the Pro Bowl seven times.

Brown finished his career with 928 catches for 12,291 yards and 83 touchdowns. That puts him at 28th, 28th, and (with Travis Kelce's next touchdown catch) 28th on the all-time list.

Which could make it hard to get him in, even without considering the off-field issues. Especially in light of the various disruptions he created for the Steelers, Raiders, Patriots, and Buccaneers.

item.title: Graham Bensinger issues statement regarding Mike Macdonald interview
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Graham Bensinger's recent interview with Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald made headlines not just for its content but for how the content was obtained — making Bensinger himself part of the story.
item.content:encoded:
Graham Bensinger's recent interview with Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald made headlines not just for its content but for how the content was obtained — making Bensinger himself part of the story.

As a result, Bensinger posted the following statement on Twitter:

"Due to ongoing media requests for comment, I want to clarify the timeline surrounding a portion of our recent interview with Mike Macdonald that has received attention this week.

"The complete Mike Macdonald interview, including the conversation now at issue, was provided to Seahawks PR last Wednesday, September 16 — five days before it was published on YouTube Monday. During that time, no concern was raised about the exchange, and we were never asked to remove it. For the last couple of years, our typical practice with long-form interview releases has been to include some of the pre-interview conversation.

"Coach Macdonald reached out to me directly yesterday morning expressing concern. I immediately told him we would remove that portion, and we did. Unfortunately, it had already been clipped from our interview by online outlets and circulated elsewhere. I told Coach that, in hindsight, I regretted allowing that exchange to be included and that it was my error in judgment.

"I have tremendous respect for Coach. We spent significant time together in Seattle, and I came away impressed not only by what he has accomplished in such a short period of time, but by the person he is. The last thing I want is for one exchange to overshadow that story. I also have great respect for Sean Payton, whom I had the opportunity to profile previously."

It will be interesting to see whether the Seahawks agree that the full conversation, including the segment regarding the 2024 brouhaha with the Broncos, was sent to them on September 16. Also, it feels like Bensinger is opting to blame the Seahawks for not spotting an interaction that, as Macdonald has said, was never meant to be aired.

Besides, why was Bensinger giving the thing to the Seahawks in advance anyway? This isn't Hard Knocks; it's an independent interview that does not need to be reviewed or approved by the subject of the interview before publication.

And while the situation has helped remind everyone that Graham Bensinger continues to operate in an increasingly crowded media space, this specific incident could complicate his efforts to attract willing participants from the NFL ecosystem for future sit-down interviews.

item.title: Mike Macdonald learned valuable lessons regarding his media approach
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Despite his immense success in a short time with one of the 32 most coveted jobs in football, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is still learning.
item.content:encoded:
Despite his immense success in a short time with one of the 32 most coveted jobs in football, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is still learning.

As it relates to his recent sit-down with Graham Bensinger, Macdonald has learned that nothing is off the record unless both sides to the conversation agree that it is. Macdonald also has learned to assume that every mic is a hot mic, and that every camera is capturing images.

He's also learning to be careful about who he trusts, and about when and where he lets himself get comfortable.

More broadly, Macdonald is learning why Bill Belichick behaves the way he does. If you say as little as possible, the chances of saying something you come to regret will be minimized.

Earlier this week, Macdonald was asked about his decision to submit to interviews in the aftermath of winning the Super Bowl.

“If someone’s interested in talking and you feel like it’s an honest process, then why not?" Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "I don’t have a long relationship with Graham [Bensinger], but I was really impressed with how they did their business. There are other podcasts that you had prior relationships with folks, and I respect the work that they do, and we have prior relationships that you want to honor. It’s probably that simple."

As the owner and operator of a media outlet, I'll never complain about coaches, players, and others from the NFL universe providing compelling content. Plenty of it comes from the press conferences to which coaches are required to submit. When they stray beyond that, they need to be careful.

Careful about what they say. Careful about who they say it to. Careful about who they trust.

As to Bensinger, he won the battle of capturing a compelling sound bite. He may have lost the broader war, however. By possibly operating under the premise that it's better to seek forgiveness than to request permission — and by clinging to the technicalities of invoking off-the-record protection — Macdonald surely won't be inclined to sit down with him again. And, if Macdonald does, he'll be far more guarded.

Others may have similar trepidations about submitting to interviews and/or allowing themselves to be charmed into getting too comfortable.

For Macdonald, he got way too comfortable. One source not connected to either the Seahawks or Broncos deemed it "reckless."

Complicating matters for Macdonald is that he now reports to ownership that didn't hire him. And while winning is ultimately all that matters, early impressions matter, too. And it's one thing for outsiders to question Macdonald's judgment and discretion. If Vinod, Neeru, and/or Neal Khosla feel a little differently about Macdonald after this incident, it could come back to haunt him if/when the wins aren't as consistent or convincing.

item.title: Sean McVay: We'll err on the side of caution with Puka Nacua
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua missed Week 2 with a groin injury and his outlook for this week's game against the Broncos remains unclear.
item.content:encoded:
Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua missed Week 2 with a groin injury and his outlook for this week's game against the Broncos remains unclear.

Head coach Sean McVay said that Nacua would have missed Wednesday's practice — the team only held a jog-through — and they'll see what he's able to do on Thursday. McVay said Nacua is "frustrated," but that the team doesn't believe this is a long-term issue and will exercise caution to ensure it doesn't become one.

“I don’t think so. I think it’s more along the lines of just seeing how that responds," McVay said, via Nate Atkins of TheAthletic.com. "When you’re a skill player and you’re really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up, then some of the things can be like pre-hernia is what he’s feeling. You err on the side of caution. Usually, time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal and then when you get to a certain point, I think you feel pretty good moving forward.”

If that doesn't happen by Sunday, Davante Adams will remain the top wide receiving option for the Rams.

item.title: Knee injury keeps Aaron Jones out of practice for Vikings
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Vikings running back Aaron Jones finished last Sunday's win over the Bears with a brace on his knee and the issue was bothering him enough on Monday that he missed practice.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings running back Aaron Jones finished last Sunday's win over the Bears with a brace on his knee and the issue was bothering him enough on Monday that he missed practice.

Jones ran 23 times for 105 yards in the 9-3 Vikings win and head coach Kevin O'Connell said that the team will we see how things play out over the next few days before making a call on Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.

“He feels great. He’s bouncing around the building like normal, but it’s more so the knee," O'Connell said at his press conference. "Just allowing that thing to turn over. He feels pretty good. We’ll just keep getting treatment around the clock and see if we can pick up his workload as the week goes on.”

Jordan Mason is on injured reserve and DeeJay Dallas was limited with a toe injury, which leaves sixth-round pick Demond Claiborne as the only healthy back on the active roster.

Linebacker Jake Golday (ankle) and punter Brett Thorson (right hamstring) also missed practice. Defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (oblique), right tackle Brian O'Neill (knee), defensive lineman Jalen Redmond (elbow), and center Nick Samac (knee) were limited participants.

item.title: Rueben Bain misses practice Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Buccaneers first-round pick Rueben Bain missed the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Buccaneers first-round pick Rueben Bain missed the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday.

Bain suffered a groin injury in last Sunday's loss to the Browns. The linebacker also dealt with a shoulder injury this summer and he has recorded one tackle on 76 snaps so far this season.

Linebackers Anthony Nelson (shin) and Josiah Trotter (shoulder) also missed practice on Wednesday. Bain and Nelson are join on the edges by Yaya Diaby, Al-Quadin Muhammad, David Walker, and Yasir Holmes.

Quarterback Baker Mayfield (illness), wide receiver Jalen McMillan (knee), and cornerback Jacob Parrish (back) were all listed as full participants ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings.

item.title: Cowboys practice without LB DeMarvion Overshown, S Malik Hooker
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys rank 29th defensively, and to add injury to insult, they have three starters and a key reserve out of practice.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys rank 29th defensively, and to add injury to insult, they have three starters and a key reserve out of practice.

Cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring), safety Malik Hooker (forearm), safety P.J. Locke (foot) and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday. That does not bode well for their availability for Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil.

Durant started the first two games and played 87 snaps; Hooker started the season opener and played only 12 snaps before his injury; Locke started the Week 2 game and has played 31 defensive snaps and 11 on special teams; and Overshown started the season opener and played 51 defensive snaps and three on special teams before his injury.

Outside linebacker James Houston (shoulder) was a full participant Wednesday.
